subject: Marketplace private offer — Acme Retail (pricing & channel splits)
messages:
From: Susan Wu <susan.wu@cloudpartner.io>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme-retail.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Marketplace private offer — Acme Retail (pricing & channel splits)

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for the call earlier. Acme is keen to move forward with a Private Offer on AWS for the enterprise bundle (100k tokens/mo baseline) but they need clarity on how the discount will flow through to the reseller and what the channel compensation structure will look like. A few specific asks from Acme procurement: 

- Confirm the list price we should publish on the AWS SKU vs the private offer price.
- Clarify what percentage of the private-offer discount is intended for Acme's reseller (they work with CloudPartner.io) vs Redwood's net.
- Confirm whether Redwood will accept a three-tiered pricing model in the private offer (baseline committed price, overage unit price, and a short-term promo on months 1–3).

Acme would like a proposed margin waterfall and a short note on whether Redwood can pass through any portion of AWS fees or if those are to be absorbed.

I've attached the procurement questionnaire and a first draft PO terms doc that Acme's legal sent over. Can you loop in your marketplace lead / finance so we can get a clean private offer draft to share with procurement next week?

Best,
Susan
Head of GTM Partnerships
CloudPartner.io

Attachments: Acme_Security_Questions.pdf (docx/pdf stub), Acme_first_PO_terms.docx (word stub)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Susan Wu <susan.wu@cloudpartner.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme-retail.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer — Acme Retail (pricing & channel splits)

Susan / team —

Thanks — this is actionable. Quick answers up front, followed by attachment references and next steps: 

1) SKU list price vs PO price: we publish a public SKU at the MSRP (recommended list price) and create the Private Offer as a discounted commitment off that SKU. For reporting we include both values on the PO so Acme sees the delta.

2) Channel compensation: Redwood is fine with a reseller commission carved out of the private-offer discount. Our standard approach is to allocate a fixed percentage of the discount to the reseller (eg. 12–18%), with Redwood keeping the remainder to cover unit economics. The precise split depends on the absolute discount size and any AWS take.

3) Three-tiered pricing: yes — we can structure baseline committed price, an overage rate, and a time-bound promo for months 1–3. We typically cap promos to avoid mismatched expectations after the promo.

Notes on AWS fees: AWS levies a transaction/seller fee and listing fee depending on the Marketplace terms. Those are generally tracked outside the discount waterfall; Redwood currently absorbs the listing admin and pays AWS from gross revenue, so the channel split should be calculated on the net after AWS marketplace fees (we can also show gross waterfall on request).

I've attached a draft commission schedule (Marketplace_Commission_Schedule.xlsx) showing a few waterfall scenarios (12/15/18% to reseller at discount levels 10/20/30%). Marissa — can you confirm the minimum net margin we need to preserve for this deal? Karthik — please review for any compliance/partner clauses that must be in the PO.

Proposed next steps:
- Internal alignment (this thread) by EOD Thu
- Final draft PO to Acme by Mon (11/30)
- DocuSign routing the week of 12/7 if procurement signoff is straight-forward

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RDW_Acme_PO_Terms_v3.pdf (pdf stub), Marketplace_Commission_Schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Susan Wu <susan.wu@cloudpartner.io>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme-retail.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer — Acme Retail (pricing & channel splits)

Rishi —

Quick internal note and constraint for the waterfall scenarios: we need to preserve at least a 28% gross margin on the committed baseline after AWS marketplace fees and reseller commission to cover SRE and support costs for an enterprise integration with SSO + audit logging. That margin floor assumes the following:

- Baseline commitment: 100k tokens/mo at a committed price of $0.012/token (example)
- AWS marketplace fee: ~8% of gross (approx, depends on listing category)
- Reseller commission target: 15% (middle case)

Attached is a simple P&L table in the spreadsheet showing net to Redwood by discount tier. If we push reseller comp >18% at a 30% private-offer discount, Redwood net margin drops below the 28% floor. 

Operational asks for PO language:
- Include an explicit clause that the reseller commission is paid by Redwood and is not a pass-through line item to be settled by Acme; Amazon only sees the final offer price.
- Specify that promo months are billed as discounted invoices but counted toward committed usage for the twelve-month term.

Karthik — flagging any partner/reseller agreement language you want included (e.g., audit rights, clawback on chargebacks).

Marissa
VP, Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Susan Wu <susan.wu@cloudpartner.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme-retail.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer — Acme Retail (pricing & channel splits)

Thanks all — this is helpful and Acme has reviewed the waterfall. They can accept a 15% reseller commission with the following conditions: 

- Private-offer discount set at 22% off MSRP for months 1–3 promo, then 18% for the remainder of the 12-month term (committed baseline).
- Reseller commission of 15% of the discount (paid by Redwood).
- Redwood confirms the 28% net margin floor (post-AWS fees and commission) in the PO terms; Acme is comfortable with the wording that the commission is paid by Redwood and not deducted from committed units for calculation of baseline usage.

Acme legal attached redlines to RDW_Acme_PO_Terms_v3.pdf; they want explicit language around data residency and audit logs. If Redwood signs these terms, Acme will issue a DocuSign for the private offer and we can route through AWS.

Please confirm you can accept the 22%/18% structure and the 15% reseller comp; if yes we'll move to DocuSign next week and share the AWS Private Offer SKU info.

Best,
Susan
Head of GTM Partnerships
CloudPartner.io

--- Forwarded attachments: RDW_Acme_PO_Terms_v3.pdf (annotated), Marketplace_Commission_Schedule.xlsx (updated)
